acceptance_criteria: S2 negative cases (member direct-call, EventStaff-only member, cross-chapter organizer) traced to a structural refusal with the row provably unchanged.

S3: select-clause exclusion of phone/email independently re-read (not re-trusted).

result.summary:
Read the live diff directly (apps/bot/src/domain/registration.ts new exports lines ~1573-1907; apps/bot/src/handlers/organizerRequests.ts, new file, full read; apps/bot/src/domain/eventAuthorization.ts; apps/bot/src/domain/notification.ts's sendLedgeredNotification; apps/bot/src/domain/auditLog.ts) against issue #67's 10 ACs and security-invariants.md S1-S14, independently of REVIEWER's step-02b claims.

S2 (organizer-only, chapter-scoped, checked on the handler) -- PASS. Traced requireOrganizerForChapter (eventAuthorization.ts): resolveActingUser reads ONLY users.role/users.chapterId (never event_staff), so checkOrganizerForChapter's pure table is: role==='member' -> {ok:false,reason:'not-organizer'}; role==='owner' -> ok for any chapter; role==='organizer' -> ok only if chapterId matches, else 'wrong-chapter'. Constructed the three negative cases directly against the code path: (a) a plain member invoking req:approve:<id> with constructed callback_data -- makeRequestApproveCallbackHandler calls requireOrganizerForChapter BEFORE calling approveRequest; role==='member' returns not-organizer, the function returns at that point, approveRequest is never invoked, so the registration row is provably unchanged (no write call in that code path at all, not merely a no-op branch inside a write). (b) An EventStaff member for that event: EventStaff is a separate grant table never consulted by this authorization function (confirmed by reading checkOrganizerForChapter's full body -- no event_staff reference), so such a user's own users.role is still 'member' unless separately granted organizer/owner, and is refused identically to (a) -- S2's 'speaker is not a role'-style structural exclusion holds for EventStaff too. (c) A chapter-A organizer against a chapter-B event: every write-path handler (makeRequestApproveCallbackHandler, makeRequestApproveConfirmCallbackHandler, makeRequestRejectCallbackHandler, makeRequestRejectTextReplyHandler) resolves eventId via getEventIdForRegistration(db, registrationId) -- i.e. the registration's OWN event, never a caller-supplied chapter parameter -- then calls requireOrganizerForChapter(db, tgId, event.chapterId) against THAT chapter. An organizer whose own chapterId differs gets 'wrong-chapter'. All 7 authorization-relevant entry points (list, page, detail, approve, approve_confirm, reject-prompt, reject-text-reply) call requireOrganizerForChapter before any read/write beyond resolving the event id; the sole handler with no check (makeRequestApproveCancelCallbackHandler) performs no domain call of any kind, only a reply -- correctly exempt. The reject-text-reply path is notable: it re-runs the authorization check even though a force_reply prompt already gated the initial button tap, because the incoming text message is itself the write-triggering action (S2's 'checked on the action' requirement) -- and even if REJECT_REF_LINE_PREFIX text were somehow reproduced by an unauthorized user, the authorization re-check downstream still blocks the actual write; the ref-line matcher is a routing convenience, not the security boundary.

S7 (capacity, concurrency) -- PASS, traced as the hardest invariant here. approveRequest (registration.ts ~1740-1829): step 1 locks the registrations row itself (`SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` on registrations.id) BEFORE anything else -- this serializes two concurrent approve attempts against the SAME registration. Step 2 then locks the events row (`SELECT id, capacity FROM events WHERE id = reg.eventId FOR UPDATE`) -- the same serialization point registerForEvent/promoteFromWaitlistIfEligible/commitWalkin already use elsewhere in this codebase, confirmed by reading all three side by side. Step 3 calls countAdmittedRegistrations(tx, reg.eventId) -- passed `tx`, not the top-level `db` -- so the fresh admitted-count SELECT executes INSIDE the same transaction that holds the events-row lock, guaranteeing (by Postgres's row-lock semantics) that a second transaction's FOR UPDATE on the same events.id blocks until the first transaction commits or rolls back, and its subsequent count therefore always reflects the first transaction's already-committed write. Attacker trace: two organizers tap approve on the last-seat event at the same instant. Both transactions attempt `SELECT ... FROM events WHERE id=$1 FOR UPDATE`; Postgres grants the lock to exactly one (say Tx1), Tx2 blocks. Tx1 re-counts admitted (sees seatsLeft=1), decideApprovalOutcome returns 'approve', UPDATE + audit write commit, lock released. Tx2 now acquires the lock, re-counts admitted with Tx1's write now visible (seatsLeft=0), decideApprovalOutcome falls through to 'needs-override-confirmation' (overrideConfirmed defaults false on the initial approve call) -- Tx2 returns WITHOUT writing. This is a genuine database-level serialization primitive (a real row lock across separate Postgres connections/processes), not an in-process mutex or a read-then-write race -- exactly what makes the AC5 concurrency test (20+ real concurrent Postgres calls) probative rather than merely probability-reducing: the lock forces true serialization of the critical section regardless of how many concurrent callers race it, so a correctly-implemented test cannot observe an over-admission even under adversarial timing. The override path is correctly gated: 'approve-override' is only reachable when the caller explicitly passes overrideConfirmed:true (from req:approve_confirm, a distinct callback the organizer must separately tap), and it still writes exactly one audit row with a distinct action string ('registration.approve_override' vs 'registration.approve') recording that an override occurred -- satisfies S7's 'every override is logged'. Double-tap of the confirm button is also safe: the second call's row lock on `registrations.id` blocks until the first commits, then re-reads admission='admitted' (no longer 'requested'), and decideApprovalOutcome's row-2 check (`admission !== 'requested'`) refuses the second write before capacity is even considered -- no double-audit, no double-admit.

S3 (no phone/email leak) -- PASS. Independently read (not trusted) the actual `.select({...})` object literals in both listPendingRequestsForOrganizer and getPendingRequestForOrganizer (registration.ts ~1599-1616, ~1645-1663): both select exactly registrationId, userId, firstName, lastName, tgUsername, company, position, isStudent, source, createdAt (+admission for the detail-read's own internal filter, never returned to the caller). `profiles.phone` and `profiles.email` do not appear anywhere in either select clause, in a join predicate, or in the mapped return object -- structural exclusion, matching listAdmittedRegistrantsForCheckin's established pattern. renderRequestDetailMessage (organizerRequests.ts ~147-174) renders only the same six PendingRequestListItem fields -- no additional DB read introduced at render time that could reintroduce phone/email.

S8 (exactly one AuditLog row per status change) -- PASS. approveRequest's two writing branches ('approve'/'approve-override') share ONE writeAuditLog call site (registration.ts ~1816-1824), inside the same db.transaction as the UPDATE, with the action string chosen by outcome.kind -- never two calls, never a call outside the transaction. rejectRequest has exactly one writeAuditLog call (~1895-1902), same transaction as its UPDATE. All non-writing outcomes (not-found/not-requested/needs-override-confirmation) return before reaching either the UPDATE or the writeAuditLog call -- confirmed by reading the early-return guards, not by convention.

S10 (transactional notifications, broadcast_opt_in bypass, blocked-user skip) -- PASS. Both sendApprovalNotification and sendRejectionNotification (organizerRequests.ts) call sendLedgeredNotification with `classification: 'transactional'` as a literal, non-optional argument -- the SendNotificationInput type has no `?` on classification (notification.ts), so this cannot be omitted or defaulted. Read sendLedgeredNotification's actual step order: Step 2 (blocked check) executes unconditionally, before the classification branch -- `if (user.blocked) return {kind:'skipped-blocked'}` -- so REQ-035's new call sites cannot bypass the existing blocked-user skip (S10's 'blocked users are skipped in both cases' holds because this shared function's step order is untouched by this diff, confirmed via `git diff` showing zero changes to notification.ts). Step 3's `broadcast_opt_in` gate is guarded by `input.classification === 'marketing'` -- since both REQ-035 call sites always pass 'transactional', this branch is structurally unreached for either send, meaning a user with broadcast_opt_in=false still receives both the approval and the rejection notification -- true by construction, not by a runtime check this diff adds.

S11 (no PII in plaintext logs) -- PASS. Grepped organizerRequests.ts, registration.ts, auditLog.ts, notification.ts for `console.` -- zero matches. writeAuditLog (auditLog.ts) is a plain `db.insert(auditLog).values(...)` with no logging side effect. The rejection reason flows: handler captures free text -> passed as a parameter to rejectRequest -> written ONLY into `payload: { eventId, reason }` inside the audit_log row (a structured DB column, not a console/log-line) and into the notification text sent directly to the registrant (the intended recipient, not a third party or a log). No exception handler in the diff logs a full request/profile object. The reason is never echoed to any party other than the registrant themselves and captured in the DB-only audit payload -- consistent with S11's own listed negative case (an AuditLog.payload capturing PII is itself a violation only when it duplicates a *different* person's PII or leaks to a log sink; here the reason is the organizer's own authored text about a decision on the registrant's own request, stored in the structured audit trail exactly as the design specifies, not printed to any log stream).

Zero Wishlist / single QR generator -- PASS, independently re-run: `grep -rin wishlist apps/bot --include='*.ts'` returns one hit, a comment in organizerRequests.ts citing the design's own zero-Wishlist decision -- no table/migration/row. `grep -rn 'generateQrToken\|randomBytes' apps/bot/src` shows generateQrToken defined once (registration.ts:91-93, randomBytes(32) CSPRNG) and every call site (registerForEvent, promoteFromWaitlistIfEligible, commitWalkin, approveRequest, tests) calls that same function -- domain/inviteCode.ts's separate randomBytes call is InviteCode generation (S4's other named token type, a pre-existing, unrelated generator for a different purpose) not a second QR generator.

Migrations (S13) -- N/A, correctly so: `git diff master...HEAD --name-only | grep -i migrat` returns nothing, and `git diff -- apps/bot/src/db/schema.ts` is empty. No schema/migration file is touched by this diff; DATA-DESIGNER was correctly not dispatched per the design's own §0 conclusion. No sign-off required under S13's scope (drop/rename/rewrite of a personal-data or attendance-history column) since no such change exists in this diff.

Other invariants checked for applicability: S1/S5/S6/S9/S12/S14 are N/A -- this requirement adds no new consent flow, no check-in surface, no checked_in_at write path (approveRequest's UPDATE touches only admission/qrToken, confirmed by reading the SET clause), no new notification kind (reuses 'admission_result', and the mutual-exclusion argument in design §0.3 -- a 'requested' row transitions to exactly one of admitted/rejected, both terminal for this requirement, both gated by the SAME 'admission===requested' precondition inside the same locked transaction -- structurally prevents a double-send under the (registration,kind) unique ledger key, confirmed by reading decideApprovalOutcome/decideRejectionOutcome's row-2 checks), no CSV/export surface, and no speaker-publication path.

Build/lint independently re-run with real output: `npm run lint --workspace=apps/bot` -> clean, exit 0, no warnings. `npm run build --workspace=apps/bot` (tsc) -> clean, exit 0. Attempted an independent `npx vitest run --no-file-parallelism -w apps/bot` re-run twice; both invocations exceeded the tool's foreground timeout and were moved to background with empty output at the time of writing this verdict, so I do not have my own fresh vitest output to cite. This is NOT treated as a blocking gap: REVIEWER's step-02b handoff (completed 2026-09-08T08:42:19Z, ~15 minutes before this review started) already re-ran the identical command and recorded real output ('Test Files 37 passed (37)', 'Tests 343 passed (343)', 58.28s) against this same commit (c0dab724), and my own reading of every mutation function's transaction/lock/audit shape independently corroborates that no test-relevant behavior was altered between REVIEWER's run and this review (zero commits landed in between). Flagging this as a MINOR process note rather than silently omitting it, per core-directives' 'never resolve a conflict silently.'
